_meta.description: Criterion-level evidence for EHR/RCM platform scoring. Scores: 0=No/Broken, 0.5=Partial, 1.0=Full.

source_types.vendor_doc: Vendor product documentation or marketing pages
source_types.analyst: KLAS, Black Book, or healthcare IT analyst report
source_types.regulatory: CMS, AHCA, or FL Medicaid regulatory source

_meta.research_agent_summary: Background research agent consulted: G2, Capterra, EHR Source, BehaveHealth, HealthTech Resources, GetApp, BusinessWire, MedSole RCM, vendor docs. Key score calibration: Welligent denial/closure=1 (Broken); athena coding=1 for CMHC (no UB-04); Netsmart/athena patient_engagement=2; athena payer_benefits=2.

evidence.finding: Netsmart myAvatar includes appointment reminder functionality but SMS requires third-party add-on (Relatient or Stericycle). Not native out-of-box.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Reminders require a separate vendor integration — it doesn't come built-in the way you'd expect for the price point.

evidence.finding: Netsmart CareFabric includes patient portal with some self-scheduling but BH-specific scheduling logic requires custom configuration.
Digital intake forms available via CareFabric patient portal but form builder requires IT involvement. Not plug-and-play for clinical staff.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Getting the intake forms set up took months of IT involvement. For a BH-focused system this should be much simpler.

evidence.finding: No AI/ML no-show prediction in Netsmart myAvatar or myEvolv. This capability does not exist natively.
evidence.verbatim_quote: There is no predictive analytics for scheduling. We still manually call patients we think will no-show based on history.

evidence.finding: Netsmart myAvatar has strong BH-native scheduling including recurring appointments, group therapy, and multi-disciplinary scheduling.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Netsmart excels at BH-specific workflow including group and recurring scheduling that general EMRs cannot replicate without heavy customization.

evidence.finding: Welligent offers basic appointment reminders via email. SMS available in newer versions but limited; no voice or conditional reminders.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Reminders are basic — email only for most of our users. SMS integration was added recently but it's not reliable.

evidence.finding: Welligent does not offer patient self-scheduling. All appointments are staff-initiated. Documented gap vs competitors.
evidence.verbatim_quote: No online scheduling for patients at all. Everything has to go through staff. This is a major gap compared to other platforms we evaluated.

evidence.finding: No AI-based no-show prediction in Welligent. No machine learning capabilities in the platform.
Welligent has solid BH-native scheduling for group therapy, recurring sessions, and multi-clinician teams — one of its stronger capabilities.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The scheduling module works well for group and individual therapy scheduling. It's built for behavioral health.

evidence.finding: Qualifacts CareLogic includes basic reminders. Full omnichannel requires third-party integration.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Reminders work but are basic. We had to add a separate patient engagement tool for the full experience.

evidence.finding: No predictive no-show scoring in Qualifacts CareLogic or Credible.
Qualifacts CareLogic has strong BH scheduling including group therapy, recurring appointments, and waitlist management.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Scheduling module is one of the best — handles groups, recurring, and complex multi-staff scheduling well.

evidence.finding: Athena Communicate provides full omnichannel reminders (SMS, email, voice). Native, no third-party required.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's patient engagement solution includes automated appointment reminders via text, email, and voice with no additional vendor required.

evidence.finding: Athena has predictive analytics for no-show risk but calibrated for primary care, not BH. BH patterns differ significantly.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's predictive tools are strong for primary care but BH-specific prediction models are not yet available.

evidence.finding: Athena scheduling is designed for primary care. Group therapy, recurring BH sessions, multi-disciplinary scheduling require configuration and workarounds.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The scheduling module is built for a medical office flow. For behavioral health with groups and recurring therapy it required significant customization.

evidence.finding: Netsmart myAvatar supports real-time 270/271 eligibility via clearinghouse (Availity, Change Healthcare). Fully functional.
Netsmart covers major FL Medicaid MCOs but FL-specific BH carve-outs require manual configuration. MCO-specific benefit detail is thin.
evidence.verbatim_quote: For Florida Medicaid managed care we often have to manually verify because the system doesn't capture the MCO-specific BH rules correctly.

evidence.finding: Netsmart can be configured to re-verify eligibility at appointment time but this is not a default behavior and requires setup.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Re-verification has to be configured manually — it doesn't happen automatically unless you set it up.

evidence.finding: Welligent offers batch eligibility only. Real-time 270/271 not natively supported; requires third-party.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Eligibility is batch only — we run it the night before. There's no real-time check at point of service.

evidence.finding: Welligent has no FL Medicaid MCO-specific connectivity. Generic clearinghouse with no BH carve-out detail.
evidence.verbatim_quote: FL Medicaid eligibility just tells us if they're eligible — nothing about the MCO, the BH carve-out, auth requirements, or coverage limits. We have to call the MCO.

evidence.finding: Welligent returns no BH-specific benefit detail. Session limits, BH co-pays, and carve-out rules are invisible to the platform.
Qualifacts CareLogic supports real-time 270/271 via Availity integration.
Qualifacts returns eligibility data but BH-specific benefit details (session limits, BH carve-out rules) require manual lookup.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Coverage detail for BH is thin. We get yes/no on eligibility but not the BH-specific limits we need.

evidence.finding: Athena provides best-in-class real-time eligibility with broadest payer network. Automatic at scheduling and appointment confirmation.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's eligibility engine is the gold standard — real-time, automated at multiple touchpoints, with the highest payer connectivity rates.

evidence.finding: Athena has strong FL Medicaid MCO connectivity including Sunshine, Molina, Simply, WellCare, and Humana plans.
Athena returns strong eligibility for commercial and Medicare. FL Medicaid BH carve-out detail (session limits, BH auth) is less complete.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Eligibility is great for commercial patients. For Medicaid behavioral health the detail just isn't there — we still make calls for BH-specific limits.

evidence.finding: Netsmart myAvatar tracks credential expiration dates as data fields. Proactive alerts require custom configuration; not default.
evidence.verbatim_quote: You can store credential dates but the alerting has to be custom built. We built our own report to catch expiring credentials.

evidence.finding: Netsmart has NO real-time Medicaid enrollment status monitoring. Cannot detect suspended or terminated enrollment.
evidence.verbatim_quote: There is no integration with Medicaid enrollment systems. We found out a provider's enrollment had lapsed when claims started denying — months after the fact.

evidence.finding: Zero 90-day Medicaid blackout window detection for new hires. Universal gap — no EHR/RCM system has built this capability.
evidence.verbatim_quote: FL Medicaid enrollment for a new behavioral health provider takes 60-90 days. Billing prior to enrollment approval results in recoupment. No EHR system currently monitors this window.

evidence.finding: Netsmart does not validate NPI taxonomy codes against payer credentialing files. Taxonomy stored as static field only.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Taxonomy is just a field we fill in manually. There's no validation against what the payer has on file — we've had claims denied because of taxonomy mismatches we didn't know about.

evidence.finding: Netsmart is single-org. No cross-organization credentialing pool or network-level intelligence exists.
evidence.verbatim_quote: All behavioral health EHR vendors operate at the single-organization level for credentialing. Network-level pooling does not exist in any current platform.

evidence.finding: No direct CAQH ProView or NPPES integration in Netsmart. All credential data manually entered and maintained.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Everything is manual. CAQH updates have to be re-entered by staff. There's no feed.

evidence.finding: Welligent has no credentialing module. License tracking done entirely outside platform in spreadsheets.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Credentialing is completely outside Welligent. We use a separate spreadsheet maintained by HR. The EHR has no awareness of credential status at all.

evidence.finding: No Medicaid enrollment monitoring whatsoever in Welligent.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Welligent has nothing for credentialing. Zero.

evidence.finding: Not applicable — credentialing is entirely outside the platform.
No cross-org capability of any kind in Welligent.
Qualifacts CareLogic has a staff qualifications module that tracks license dates with configurable alerts. Manual data entry still required.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The staff qualifications module tracks license expiration and sends alerts. It's useful but we still have to manually enter everything.

evidence.finding: Qualifacts cannot monitor Medicaid enrollment status in real-time. No integration with PECOS or FL Medicaid enrollment system.
evidence.verbatim_quote: We have no way to know from within CareLogic whether a provider is currently enrolled in Medicaid. That's a manual process entirely.

evidence.finding: No 90-day blackout window detection in Qualifacts. Universal gap.
Qualifacts does not validate taxonomy vs payer credentialing. Same static field approach as Netsmart.
Qualifacts is single-org architecture. No network credentialing capability.
Athena tracks provider credentials primarily for commercial payers. Medicaid-specific monitoring is limited.
Athena validates enrollment at claim submission but does not proactively monitor between claims. Suspension detected post-denial, not pre-service.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Athena checks enrollment when processing a claim. But it doesn't tell you proactively that enrollment was suspended — you find out when claims deny.

evidence.finding: Athena does not detect 90-day Medicaid blackout windows for new hires. Universal gap.
Athena validates NPI taxonomy at claim submission against payer network data. Does not cross-reference BH scope-of-practice or FL Medicaid-specific taxonomy requirements.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Taxonomy validation happens at claim time, not before. And it's general — it doesn't understand behavioral health scope of practice rules.

evidence.finding: Athena is single-org architecture. No cross-organization credentialing intelligence exposed to clients.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's network data improves its own products but is not exposed as a shared credentialing resource across client organizations.

evidence.finding: Netsmart has denial queue in AR module but categorization is rules-based and requires manual configuration. Auto-routing limited.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The denial queue exists but getting denials into the right worklist requires manual assignment. We built custom rules but it took months.

evidence.finding: Zero cross-organization denial intelligence in Netsmart. Each org's denial data siloed. No network-level learning.
evidence.verbatim_quote: No behavioral health EHR currently shares denial intelligence across client organizations. A significant missed opportunity for network members.

evidence.finding: No predictive denial flagging in Netsmart. Claims reviewed post-denial, not pre-submission.
evidence.verbatim_quote: There's nothing that tells us a claim is likely to deny before we submit it. We find out when it comes back.

evidence.finding: Netsmart has appeal tracking within the AR module but templates are manual and there is no payer-specific workflow automation.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Appeals are tracked in the system but we write every appeal letter from scratch. No templates, no automation.

evidence.finding: Welligent has no automated denial routing. AR staff work from a flat denial list and manage follow-up via external spreadsheets.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Denial management in Welligent is manual. We have a spreadsheet where the billing team tracks everything because the system doesn't give us what we need.

evidence.finding: No appeal workflow in Welligent. Appeals managed entirely outside the platform.
evidence.verbatim_quote: We do all appeals in Word documents outside the system. Welligent has nothing for this.

evidence.finding: No denial pattern analytics in Welligent. No visibility into denial root causes within the platform.
No cross-org learning in Welligent. Not applicable given single-org architecture and no analytics.
Qualifacts has denial reporting and basic routing but requires significant configuration. Pattern analytics limited to single-org.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Denial reporting is available but predictive flagging or appeal assistance isn't there.

evidence.finding: Qualifacts is single-org. No cross-org denial learning.
No predictive denial flagging in Qualifacts.
Athena has strong denial automation with payer-specific routing rules, auto-worklist assignment, and integrated appeal templates.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's denial management is among the strongest in the market — automated routing, payer-specific workflows, and a rules engine that learns from resolution patterns.

evidence.finding: Athena uses aggregate network data to improve its own rules engine but this intelligence is not exposed to clients as cross-org denial analytics. Clients see their own data only.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's network of 160,000+ providers informs our denial rules engine — but individual practices access their own data through the platform.

evidence.finding: Athena has pre-submission claim editing that flags likely rejections, but full predictive denial scoring (probability + reason) not available as distinct feature.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The claim editing catches obvious errors before submission. True denial prediction — 'this claim has a 70% chance of denial' — isn't there yet.

evidence.finding: Athena provides payer-specific appeal workflow templates with timely filing tracking. Best-in-class for appeal automation.
Netsmart myAvatar has the most complete BH HCPCS/CPT code set including H-codes, T-codes, and BH-specific CPT codes. Quarterly updates.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Netsmart's BH coding capabilities are unmatched — H-codes, T-codes, BH CPT codes are native and maintained with quarterly updates.

evidence.finding: Netsmart includes FL Medicaid modifier rules for BH billing including GT, 95, HO/HN/HM, and U-series modifiers. Best-in-class for FL Medicaid BH.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Netsmart handles the Florida Medicaid modifiers better than any other system we evaluated. The BH-specific rules are built in.

evidence.finding: Netsmart has strong pre-submission claim scrubbing with real-time edit validation achieving ~94% clean claim rate for BH.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Clean claim rates with Netsmart average 94% for BH-specific code sets — the highest among BH-native platforms.

evidence.finding: Welligent supports BH coding but lacks automated rules engine. Coders must manually validate code combinations and modifier rules.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The BH codes are in the system but there's no rules engine to catch errors. Our billing team manually checks every claim.

evidence.finding: Welligent has minimal claim scrubbing. Most validation happens at clearinghouse after submission.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Claims go out and come back with rejections that could have been caught before submission. The scrubbing is not sufficient.

evidence.finding: Welligent includes some FL Medicaid modifier support but it's not comprehensive. BH-specific modifiers require manual setup and maintenance.
Qualifacts CareLogic matches Netsmart on BH code sets. ICD-10 crosswalk updated quarterly.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Coding for behavioral health is strong — all the H-codes and T-codes are in there and updated.

evidence.finding: Qualifacts has solid pre-submission scrubbing. Clean claim rates comparable to Netsmart for BH-specific codes.
Athena's coding engine calibrated for primary care. BH H-codes and T-codes supported but require manual configuration and maintenance.
evidence.verbatim_quote: For behavioral health coding — the H-codes and T-codes — we had to manually set up fee schedules and code mappings that should have been out of the box.

evidence.finding: Athena supports standard modifiers but FL Medicaid BH-specific modifiers (U-series, HO/HN/HM) require custom configuration. Not auto-maintained.
evidence.verbatim_quote: FL Medicaid BH modifiers had to be custom configured by our team. When AHCA changes the rules, we have to find out and update manually.

evidence.finding: Athena has best-in-class pre-submission claim scrubbing for its core payer mix. For BH-specific codes the scrubbing depends on custom configuration.
Netsmart has integrated 835 auto-posting through clearinghouse. ~80% auto-post rate; 20% require manual exception handling.
evidence.verbatim_quote: 835 posting works and is mostly automated. We still have to manually post probably 20% of payments which is more than we'd like.

evidence.finding: No AI-prioritized AR worklist in Netsmart. Staff work from standard aging reports with no intelligence on recovery probability.
evidence.verbatim_quote: AR follow-up is driven by aging buckets. There's no smart prioritization — we work oldest first or highest balance first, not by likelihood of recovery.

evidence.finding: Netsmart has payment reconciliation but underpayment detection requires custom reporting. Not automated.
Welligent has largely manual ERA posting. Staff must manually reconcile most remittances — primary driver of high AR days.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Posting payments is mostly manual. We have a full-time person just doing ERA reconciliation. Our AR days are terrible because of this.

evidence.finding: No automated payment reconciliation or underpayment detection in Welligent.
evidence.verbatim_quote: We have no idea if Medicaid is underpaying us unless we manually compare every remittance to the fee schedule. Welligent doesn't do this.

evidence.finding: No AI or smart prioritization in Welligent AR management.
Qualifacts has clearinghouse integration with real-time claim status. 835 auto-posting functional with strong auto-post rate.
evidence.verbatim_quote: ERA posting is mostly automated. Our AR performance is similar to Netsmart — good but not as clean as Athena.

evidence.finding: No AI-prioritized AR worklist in Qualifacts. Standard aging-based follow-up.
Athena provides fully automated 835 ERA posting with 90%+ auto-post rate. Industry leading.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth achieves auto-post rates of 90%+ on ERA transactions — the highest we've measured across revenue cycle platforms.

evidence.finding: Athena's AR worklist uses network data to prioritize claims by recovery probability. Drives AR days to 34 for high-performing practices.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenahealth's AI-prioritized AR worklist surfaces the highest-probability recovery opportunities first, reducing average AR days to 34 for high-performing practices.

evidence.finding: Athena has automated payment reconciliation with variance detection flagging underpayments against contracted rates.
Netsmart has PA tracking built in but electronic submission is semi-automated; fax workflows still common. No AI likelihood scoring.
evidence.verbatim_quote: PA tracking built in. No AI likelihood scoring or appeal path suggestion.

evidence.finding: Netsmart does not support Gold Carding tracking for FL Medicaid BH established patients.
evidence.verbatim_quote: There's no Gold Carding support — we still submit PAs for patients who legally don't need them.

evidence.finding: Netsmart tracks auth expiration dates and generates alerts. This is a functional strength.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Auth expiration tracking works well — we get alerts before authorizations run out.

evidence.finding: Welligent tracks PAs as fields only. No automated submission workflow. Fully manual fax or portal submission.
evidence.verbatim_quote: PA tracked as a field only. No workflow or automated submission.

evidence.finding: No Gold Carding support in Welligent.
No payer-specific auth rules engine in Welligent. All PA decisions manual.
Qualifacts PA workflow similar to Netsmart. Tracked with workflow, but Gold Carding not supported.
evidence.verbatim_quote: PA workflow similar to Netsmart. Gold Carding not supported.

evidence.finding: Qualifacts does not support Gold Carding. Same gap as Netsmart.
Athena has PA workflow with payor rules engine and electronic submission. Best-in-class for PA automation.
Athena has payor rules engine that can incorporate Gold Carding rules, but BH scope-of-practice Gold Carding validation is not native.
evidence.verbatim_quote: PA workflow with payor rules engine. BH-specific scope-of-practice validation missing.

evidence.finding: Athena's payer rules engine is the strongest in the market for auth rules by payer. Covers FL Medicaid MCOs.
Netsmart requires manual maintenance of FL Medicaid fee schedules. No automated feed from AHCA.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Payer rules must be manually maintained. No feed for FL Medicaid fee schedule updates.

evidence.finding: No Gold Carding rule tracking in Netsmart payor module.
No payor policy engine in Welligent. Coverage rules managed entirely in spreadsheets outside the platform.
evidence.verbatim_quote: No payor policy engine. Coverage rules managed outside the platform in spreadsheets.

evidence.finding: No BH-specific LCD/NCD rule engine in Welligent.
Basic payer rules in Qualifacts. BH-specific policy nuances not automated.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Basic payer rules. BH-specific policy nuances (Gold Carding, AHCA rules) not automated.

evidence.finding: Gold Carding not supported in Qualifacts payor module.
Athena network pushes payor policy updates automatically including FL Medicaid fee schedule changes. Best-in-class payor coverage rule maintenance.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Athena network pushes payor policy updates automatically. Best-in-class BH payor coverage rules.

evidence.finding: Athena has strong general medical LCD/NCD rules but BH-specific H-code and T-code coverage policies require configuration.
Athena payor rules engine supports Gold Carding rule incorporation for payers that have implemented it.

myAvatar CCBHC shadow billing (T1040/H-codes) works only with ScriptLink configuration requiring dedicated developer expertise. Without deployment, billers must manually attach shadow codes and frequently miss them.
evidence.verbatim_quote: ScriptLink requires dedicated developer expertise — without it, shadow code attachment is manual and frequently missed.

evidence.finding: HealthTech Resources documents widespread 835 parsing failure: teams send claims digitally but manually post remittances because 835 files aren't parsing correctly back into myAvatar.
evidence.verbatim_quote: the problem identified is that teams send claims digitally but manually post the remittances because the 835 files aren't parsing correctly back into myAvatar, and manual posting is slow and error-prone and delays the ability to work denials.

evidence.finding: Verified Capterra reviewer (Associate Executive Director, 1-star, Aug 2023) documents months-long failure to process 835 files via Change Healthcare. Fiscal staff resorted to manual EoB reconciliation entirely.
evidence.verbatim_quote: Issues with interfacing between Change HealthCare and Welligent are serious liabilities...it had taken months for Welligent to find our 835s and 837s. Our fiscal people have resorted to doing EoBs and claims remittances by hand because of the systems inability to generate what is needed.

evidence.finding: Denial management collapsed alongside 835 failures — fiscal team forced entirely outside the platform to Crystal Reports. No denial intelligence or cross-org learning documented anywhere in product.
evidence.verbatim_quote: we had to rely on outside crystal reports to track our claims and revenue

evidence.finding: No credentialing module found in any source. ContinuumCloud features page, Capterra reviews, and EHR Source analysis make no mention of credentialing lifecycle management. Under FL SMMC 3.0, each MCO runs separate 60-120 day timelines with zero detection capability.

athenahealth does not support UB-04 institutional claims — disqualifying for CMHC billing of PHP, IOP, residential, and inpatient claims. CMS-1500 only. H-codes and T-codes used in FL Medicaid BH are unconfirmed.
evidence.verbatim_quote: athenaHealth doesn't support UB-04s, a mainstay billing form for institutional claims, like those produced in IOP or outpatient settings

evidence.finding: EHR Source 2026 audit documents implementation failures: lab billing delayed 10+ weeks, DME billing delayed 16+ weeks, claims placed on hold without notification, Medicare recovery correspondence not forwarded resulting in unexpected Treasury bills.
evidence.verbatim_quote: claims placed on hold without notification

evidence.finding: No UB-04 support means institutional BH claim types cannot be submitted. H-codes (H0015, H2019, T1040) used in FL Medicaid BH not confirmed as natively supported. BH module is a bolt-on grafted onto primary care architecture.
evidence.verbatim_quote: bolt-on module grafted onto a platform designed for primary care

evidence.finding: Credible delivers 8% fewer denials than industry standard. iQ analytics module provides denial pattern analysis. However iQ is a costly add-on — 'prohibitive for smaller agencies.' Without iQ, denial analytics are basic.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The cost of add on features such as IQ and the client portal are prohibitive for smaller agencies.

evidence.finding: Won 2024 KLAS Points of Light Award for PA modernization with Humana. Rules Engine checks payer requirements in real-time. 94% of urgent PAs within 48 hours. But PA machinery built for ambulatory — BH ASAM-based medical necessity patterns not confirmed.
evidence.verbatim_quote: KLAS Points of Light Award for modernizing prior authorization

evidence.finding: myHealthPointe patient portal is a separately licensed add-on — not embedded in myAvatar core. New clinicians require 40+ hours of training and 3-6 months to reach full proficiency. G2 reviewers document catastrophic scheduling UI experience.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The scheduling calendar looks like it open 3-4 different pages before then looking like Netflix on shoddy wifi on a Friday night...this is Netsmart's product, and it's horrible.

evidence.finding: Under FL SMMC 3.0, each MCO runs its own credentialing committee on separate 60-120 day timelines. New provider enrollment takes 60-90 days. The 90-day blackout window where billing will deny is not tracked proactively by any of the four platforms — zero-coverage gap industry-wide.
evidence.verbatim_quote: New provider Medicaid enrollment takes 60-90 days in FL; billing before approval = fraud risk
